clue.text: Ties arranged during Football Association's Spanish holiday

indicators.note: during places the reworked letters within the span of the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: FA is the standard abbreviation for the Football Association, English football's governing body

indicators.note: ties that have been arranged are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A football body's sides are drawn against each other while Spain has a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ties' reads as matches in a football cup draw, but its letters are the anagram fodder for 'arranged', and 'during' sets the result within the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a religious feast day or public festival in Spain and Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Supporter has portable window over door

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or performer
light, as in lightweight, describes something easily carried

explanation.surface: A fan brings along a carry-around window to fit above the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is the semicircular or rectangular pane set above a doorway to let light into a hall.

clue.text: Not difficult departing — and relaxed

parts.note: easy means not difficult
going means leaving or departing

explanation.surface: Someone leaving without trouble, and feeling calm about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going person is relaxed and tolerant, not easily upset.

clue.text: Take new wood

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of take are made into something new, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick up some fresh timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is the hard, durable timber of a tropical Asian tree, prized for furniture and boats.

clue.text: Work a long time on twitch, like Carmen

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
an era is a long period of time
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone toils for ages at a nervous habit, in the manner of a famous gypsy heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen is Bizet's opera, so the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is an opera, so something like it is in the manner of opera.

clue.text: Aspired, wrongly, to be admired

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of aspired are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone who aimed high, but mistakenly, simply to be looked up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges ASPIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be praised is to be spoken of with approval, which is to be admired.

clue.text: Politesse could be about splendid chaps taking time

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
fine means splendid or excellent
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Good manners might concern fine fellows who take their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is formal politeness, and refinement is polish and good breeding in manners.

clue.text: To begin with the women are now going to strum

indicators.note: to begin with tells us to take just the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: First the ladies are about to play a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To begin with' takes the first letters of 'the women are now going'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the ringing sound of a plucked string, and to twang a guitar is to strum or pluck it.

clue.text: First letter in the island? Make a fuss!

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about how a word on a Greek island begins, then a demand for a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside CRETE. To create is British informal for making a fuss or kicking up a row.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to create means to complain noisily or make a scene.

clue.text: Getting on? Take a good drug and gin cocktail

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a pill and a gin cocktail at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, which is what ageing describes.

clue.text: Go in last with a strange feeling for the past

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters have been made strange, put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Advice to bat last, bringing an odd emotion along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges GO IN LAST plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for times gone by.

clue.text: Sweetheart becoming to finger silk fabric

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sweetheart becoming to finger silk fabric': FLAME (sweetheart) is F + LAME (fabric), but no word gives F; 'becoming to finger' looks like an OCR misreading of 'beginning to finger', more than three letters off, and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sweetheart becoming to finger silk fabric

clue.text: Shakespearean villain -one in the past

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A stage bad guy, a figure from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain who destroys Othello in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Wood Street thing ruined opening

parts.note: fir is a type of wood

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of thing are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Something on a leafy street has been spoiled at its launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns THING into NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A first night is the opening performance of a play or show.

clue.text: Teams go off riding this way?

parts.note: sides are teams in a match
eggs addle when they go off or turn rotten

explanation.surface: Asks whether teams that turn bad are horse-riding in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: To addle is to go rotten, said of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidesaddle is a way of riding a horse with both legs on one side, traditionally by women in skirts.

clue.text: Greeting bits of ice falling

definitions.meaning: when pellets of ice fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A hello delivered as frozen pellets come down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailing means both calling a greeting and a shower of ice pellets coming down.

clue.text: Very annoyed about request for table linen

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for very annoyed is read backwards

parts.note: mad means very annoyed
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone fuming over a demand for a tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MAD into DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned woven fabric traditionally used for tablecloths and napkins.

clue.text: Something special in cow pies he cooked ?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of cow pies he are messed about with

explanation.surface: A hint of something remarkable among the beef pies a man has baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges COW PIES HE. Cow pies are the comic-strip meal of Desperate Dan.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding example displayed for admiration, something special.

clue.text: Set out to wander and alienate

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are knocked out of order

parts.note: to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: Setting out on a ramble and pushing people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone hostile or distant, to alienate them.

clue.text: A desire that's excessive? That's OK

parts.note: greed is an excessive desire for more

explanation.surface: Someone asks if their appetite is too much, and is told it's fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed is said to accept a proposal, much like saying that's fine.

clue.text: Doctor a thug disturbed for medicine

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of a thug are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A physician treats an agitated thug with medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges A THUG into AUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a dose of liquid medicine to be drunk.

clue.text: Outlaw joseph's string instruments

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
Joe is the familiar short form of the name Joseph, so Joseph's becomes Joe's

explanation.surface: Banning a man named Joseph's guitars and fiddles.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: Joe's gives JOES. BANJOES is an accepted plural beside BANJOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Banjos are stringed instruments with a drum-like body, plucked or strummed.

clue.text: Giselle put everything into gamble

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone stakes the lot on a famous romantic ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... into' signals the container. Giselle is a classic romantic ballet by Adam, so the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Giselle is a celebrated romantic work of classical dance, an example of the form.

clue.text: Bit dessert

definitions.meaning: a ... is a small amount, a bit, as in a ... late
a layered pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.walkthrough: Trifle is a British dessert of sponge soaked in sherry with fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifle means both a small amount and the British layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream.

clue.text: Possible to do it again with salesman on each stall?

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman
a table at a market can serve as a stall

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sales rep could rerun something at a market stall, each in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatable describes something that can be done or said again.

clue.text: Nothing in drink which makes sense

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: There is no drink here that makes any sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of something is its meaning or purpose, as in seeing the sense of it.

clue.text: Pole hits back

indicators.note: back means the word for hits is read backwards

parts.note: raps are hits or knocks

explanation.surface: A man from Poland strikes in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAPS into SPAR. 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, especially one used as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Popular cold and hot measure

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trendy gauge for temperatures both cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, a measure of twelfths of a foot.

clue.text: Day editor got hot

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor overheated one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has fried has been cooked in hot fat, so it has become hot.

clue.text: Head goes after fresh vegetable

indicators.note: goes after says the word for head is placed after the next piece

parts.note: green means fresh or new
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone's mind turns to finding new veg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes after' fixes the order of the two pieces. Bean is informal British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Green beans are the edible unripe pods of the common bean, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Take some food into foyer for appeal

indicators.note: into places one piece within another

parts.note: an entry is an entrance hall or foyer
to eat is to take some food

explanation.surface: Someone asks to bring a snack into the lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'foyer' stands for an entrance hall rather than a theatre lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, an appeal.

clue.text: Important person's food

definitions.meaning: an important person, so the clue reads important person is
a food made from milk curds

explanation.surface: The fare eaten by somebody grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese means a dairy food, and in big cheese, a self-important bigwig.
